claims.text: A 100–500 nm conformal h-BN coating can be deposited on cast or wrought CoCrFeNi by chemical vapor deposition.
The deposited h-BN film will adhere to the CoCrFeNi substrate.
h-BN has a layered structure with weak interlayer van der Waals forces.
The layered h-BN film provides a lubricious sliding interface.
The h-BN coating reduces interfacial shear through its layered structure.
h-BN has sufficient thermal stability to preserve a lubricious state during sliding up to 800 °C.
h-BN has sufficient chemical stability to preserve a lubricious state during high-temperature sliding.
The h-BN coating mitigates oxidation and sliding-induced degradation of CoCrFeNi.
Coated CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
Coated CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
The predicted friction and wear improvements result from persistence of the lubricious h-BN interface.
Uncoated CoCrFeNi tends to experience relatively high friction.
Uncoated CoCrFeNi tends to experience relatively high wear rates, especially at elevated temperatures.
The hypothesis is scoped to sliding loads of approximately 10–100 N, temperatures from room temperature to 800 °C, and ambient-air or inert environments.
Strongly oxidizing environments may require an adhesion-promoting interlayer.
At the upper temperature limit, particularly under oxidizing conditions, the ultrathin h-BN film may degrade or delaminate.

Coating integrity, friction, wear, oxidation state, and phase stability can be evaluated using continuous friction measurement, mass loss or profilometry, microscopy, thermal analysis, XRD, and surface spectroscopy.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant improvement of approximately 20% in both friction and wear relative to an uncoated control is designated as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies h-BN coating alone, whereas the experiment permits an optional adhesion-promoting interlayer. Including that interlayer only for coated specimens would change the tested intervention and prevent clean attribution of performance to h-BN alone.
